meta.name: ProjectLens independent held-out set 5
meta.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 for source data and verbatim government narratives; independently authored labels and explanations.
meta.yearConvention: prevYear/year are annual-report release years. Source release fields name the financial-year releases. Older releases generally report the preceding September; the 2021 release compares against the September 2019 snapshot published in 2020.
meta.narrative: Complete current-release schedule cell, with original spelling, punctuation and whitespace. No paraphrases, generated variants or invented dates.
meta.labelling: C2 rules. Explicitly stated end-date movements are explained. A moved date with an unchanged/on-track claim or an unexplained conflicting current end date is a contradiction. Equal dates are no-move unless the commentary names a different current end/closure date, in which case published-date-check.
meta.independence: No tool implementation, tests or engine files read. Neither tool was run. Prior bench JSON and input data read only to identify exclusions and the required format.
meta.exclusion: Excludes every matched prior project name and GMPP ID from sets 1–4 and the allowed input directories. Matching propagates known ID/name links across releases; historical renames used in selected pairs are documented in matchedBy.

cases.narrative: The Programme has continued to make good progress with all core components of the system now underway and in the delivery pipeline. The Programme has now implemented the system to its Full Business Case partners as well as consuming a number of new Brexit-driven Partners. The Programme agreed with the IPA in autumn 2017 that end March 2019 is an achievable target date for Programme closure.  The Service Organisation is well established and is increasingly picking up work transitioning from the Programme.  The Target Operating Model aims to deliver significant Programme transition to the DfID organisation managing the Service through 2018.

cases.narrative:
Compared to financial year 23/24-Q4, the project's end-date at 24/25-Q4 increased from 28/10/2024 to 30/05/2025. This is primarily due to the following factors‚
The conclusion of the Visa and Citizenship Application Service (VCAS) procurement was delayed due to a legal challenge to the procurement outcome by a bidder (which was later dropped). The Programme was expected to award contracts in July 2023, however the legal challenge put a suspension on the contract awards for three of the five contracts. FSS was able to award one contract in August 2023 and was successful in October 2023 in lifting the suspension of award in the remaining contracts. Once all five contracts had been awarded, the Programme worked closely with the new commercial partners at detailed implementation planning and revisited its delivery timelines, shifting Programme closure to March 2025. A Portfolio Change Request in July 2024 included an additional two months of Early Life Support resulting in Programme closure timelines extending to May 2025.
cases.label: explained
cases.why: The narrative explicitly gives the extension to May 2025 and describes procurement litigation, revised implementation planning and two months of early-life support.

cases.narrative: In August 2016 an Outline Business Case Addendum was approved to deliver a refined hybrid model so that the NHS Business Services Authority undertake Payroll Administration services in addition to Pensioner Administration, insourcing from the incumbent supplier with transitional support provided in line with contractual exit provisions. Pensioner Administration and Payroll responsibilities transferred to the NHS Business Services Authority on 2 July 2018, completing the insourcing activities, and successfully delivering against the original programme objectives. The programme has remained on GMPP after closure pending independent assurance that the benefits have successfully been delivered
cases.label: published-date-check
cases.why: The published end stays at 21 July 2017, while the narrative explicitly says the project closure moved to 21 July 2018. The date field and closure commentary disagree.

cases.project: NOMS ICTS Services (NIS) Programme (formally part of Quantum Re-compete Project)
cases.narrative:
Deployment of the main rollout activities was paused between August and December 2014, whilst significant performance issues were investigated and corrected. 

The revised remediation plan agreed by the Programme Board, sets out the new phased approach to delivery. This has had significant impact on the schedule, moving the main rollout and programme closure into 2015/16.
